title: An iterable range
description:
Write a `Range` class that works with `for...of` and the spread operator.

```
[...new Range(1, 5)]        -> [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
[...new Range(10, 0, -5)]   -> [10, 5, 0]
new Range(1, 10).includes(4) -> true
[...new Range(1, 10, 3).map(n => n * n)] -> [1, 16, 49, 100]
```
hints: Counting down needs a different loop test: `step > 0 ? n <= this.end : n >= this.end` (lesson 3.04).
`includes` checks that `n` is between the ends and that `(n - start) % step === 0`.
requirements: `new Range(start, end, step = 1)` includes `end` when the steps land on it.
A step of 0 throws `RangeError("step cannot be 0")`.
`includes(n)` works without making an array; `map(fn)` returns a generator.
stretch: Add `filter(fn)` and `take(count)`, so `new Range(1, Infinity).filter(isPrime).take(5)` gives the first five primes.
